reasoning: The AC01 rejection indicates an invalid account number; the IBAN’s check digits failed, which is typical of a data‑entry mistake. German IBAN formats have not changed, so a format migration is unlikely. A past case (M1) with the same rejection was caused by a transposed digit, supporting a typo explanation.
recommended_action: Contact the client to verify the IBAN ******************1702, correct any digit errors, and resubmit the payment. If the client confirms the IBAN is correct, request a confirmation from the beneficiary bank.

prevention_tip: Implement an automated IBAN validation check in the payment entry system to catch digit errors before submission.
